lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
Canadians will bow their heads to honour those who served and sacrificed for their country as they gather across the country to mark Remembrance Day, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday.
Stellantis has officially signed an agreement with defence contractor Roshel to sell its Brampton, Ont., assembly plant that has been idle for years, The Canadian Press reports.

A large-scale prisoner exchange emerged as the only tangible result of two days of US-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, with no breakthrough on a ceasefire or territorial disputes. #EuropeNews, Euronews reports.

Just six years after Mississippi removed the Confederate stars and bars from its state flag, Scott Colom could become the first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction and the first Democrat to win the seat since 1982, The Canadian Press reports.
House Republicans consider issuing subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, ABC News reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
